podcast.title: Overdubbed "I'll Come Running Back to You"
podcast.body: After the legal disputes, Art Rupe hired The Lee Gotch Singers to overdub Sam Cooke's demo "I'll Come Running Back to You" to make it sound like "You Send Me," despite his prior strong objections to their involvement. "Roup...got many hall and the Lee got singers. The very people whose work on You Send Me and Sumitain, he despised so much. To record overdubbs, to make it sound as much like You Send Me as possible."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty: "You Send Me" by Sam Cooke

podcast.title: Source of Art Rupe's Outrage
podcast.body: Art Rupe was "horrified" by the decision to use white backing vocalists, especially women, behind Sam Cooke's vocals, believing it diluted the "black music" sound he sought for Specialty Records. "Rube was horrified that bumps and bathees had put white backing vocalists behind Cooke's vocals."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty: "You Send Me" by Sam Cooke

podcast.title: White Backing Vocal Group
podcast.body: The Lee Gotch Singers were a white vocal group, highly sought after in Los Angeles, who provided backing vocals on Sam Cooke's "You Send Me" session. "on backing vocals were the Lee Gotch Singers, a white vocal group who were among the most in-demand vocalists in LA."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
